policy_name: Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security Act of 2024
question: What are the specific conditions under which a person 'reasonably should have known' of the unauthorized use of an individual's voice or likeness, as stipulated in Section 11 of the Act, for them to be held liable?
answer_low_temp: A person'reasonably should have known' of the unauthorized use of an individual's voice or likeness if they had knowledge or, in the absence of knowledge, if they should have known based on reasonable circumstances. policy_name: California AI-ware Act
question: What specific enforcement actions or penalties are outlined in the California AI-ware Act for state agencies failing to clearly identify generative AI interactions or provide alternative human contact options?
answer_low_temp:
The California AI-ware Act does not explicitly outline specific enforcement actions or penalties for state agencies failing to clearly identify generative AI interactions or provide alternative human contact options. However, it is stated in Section 11549.84(a) that a state agency that utilizes generative artificial intelligence to directly communicate with a person, either through an online interface or telephonically, shall clearly and in a conspicuous manner identify to that person that their interaction with the state agency is being communicated through artificial intelligence. Additionally, Section 11549.84(b) requires a state agency to provide clear instructions, or a link to a page with clear instructions, informing the person when and how the person can directly communicate with a person from the state agency. The Office of Artificial Intelligence, established in Section 11549.82, has the power and authority necessary to guide the design, use, or deployment of automated systems by a state agency to ensure compliance with these requirements (Section 11549.83). The specific enforcement actions or penalties for non-compliance are not specified in the Act.

Sources:

However, it does state that the Office of Artificial Intelligence has the power and authority necessary to guide the design, use, or deployment of automated systems by a state agency to ensure compliance (Section 11549.83). answer_low_temp: Under the California AI-ware Act, a state agency utilizes generative artificial intelligence to directly communicate with a person if the AI system is used to interact with a natural person (i.e., a human) through an online interface or telephonically. policy_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination")
question: How will the working group ensure that knowledge and technical data produced by member countries remains under their respective export control laws and regulations, as stipulated in Section 1087(d)?

Citation: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Sec. 1087.

policy_name: AI Ads Act
question: What are the potential penalties or enforcement actions for individuals or entities found to be in violation of the AI Ads Act's provisions regarding the fraudulent use of AI-generated content in political campaigns?
answer_low_temp:
The AI Ads Act does not explicitly outline the penalties or enforcement actions for individuals or entities found to be in violation of its provisions regarding the fraudulent use of AI-generated content in political campaigns. However, it amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (FECA) to include AI-generated content under the existing prohibitions against fraudulent misrepresentation and solicitation of funds.

Under the FECA, violations can result in civil penalties, criminal penalties, or both. Civil penalties can range from $500 to $20,000 for each violation, with the maximum penalty for a series of related violations being $70,000. Criminal penalties can include fines and imprisonment.

For more information on the penalties for violations of the FECA, please refer to Title 52 of the United States Code, Subtitle I, Part III, Chapter 30, Subchapter II, Section 30109 - Civil penalties and Section 30110 - Criminal penalties.

question: To what extent does the AI Ads Act's extension of prohibitions against fraudulent misrepresentation apply to communications made by individuals or groups not directly affiliated with a candidate or committee?
answer_low_temp:
The AI Ads Act extends the prohibition against fraudulent misrepresentation to apply to any candidate, political party, or other real or fictitious political committee or organization, or employee or agent of such a candidate, political party, or political committee or organization (Sec. 3(a)(1), Sec. 3(b)). This means that the Act applies to communications made by individuals or groups not directly affiliated with a candidate or committee, as long as they are representing or soliciting funds for a candidate, political party, or political committee or organization. This means that the prohibition applies to communications made by individuals or groups not directly affiliated with a candidate or committee, as long as they are a candidate, political party, or political committee or organization, or an employee or agent of such.

policy_name: Digital Defense Content Provenance Act of 2023
question: What specific measures will the Director of the Defense Media Activity take to ensure the successful establishment and implementation of the digital content provenance course of education at DINFOS, and what are the reporting requirements to Congress regarding this implementation?
answer_low_temp:
The Director of the Defense Media Activity (DMA) will establish a course of education at the Defense Information School (DINFOS) to teach practical concepts and skills needed by public affairs, audiovisual, visual information, and records management specialists regarding digital content provenance. The course will cover challenges posed to Department missions and operations by a digital content forgery, the development of industry open technical standards for verifying digital content provenance, hands-on training techniques, post-production tasks, and other matters as the Director considers appropriate (Sec. 2(b)(1)-(2)).

To ensure the successful establishment and implementation of the digital content provenance course of education, the DMA will need to have the appropriate expertise and qualifications among the Department personnel responsible for teaching the course. The DMA will also need to consult and use a list of sources to develop the curriculum for the course (Sec. 2(b)(1)(A)-(B)).

The DMA will provide a report to the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives one year after the establishment of the course, detailing the status of the development of a curriculum, the implementation plan, the resources available, and whether the Director requires any additional resources (Sec. 2(b)(3)).

Citation: S. 2222, Digital Defense Content Provenance Act of 2023, Sec. 2(b)(1)-(3)
answer_high_temp: The Director of the Defense Media Activity will establish a course of education at DINFOS to teach practical concepts and skills needed by public affairs, audiovisual, visual information, and records management specialists. This course will cover challenges posed by digital content forgery, industry open technical standards for verifying digital content provenance, hands-on training techniques, post-production tasks, and other matters as deemed appropriate. Within one year of the course's establishment, the Director is required to provide a report to the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives, detailing the status of the development of the curriculum, the implementation plan, resources available, and any additional resources required (Section 2(b)(3)).
